Let \(N=100a+10b+c\), with \(a\in\{1,\dots,9\}\), \(b,c\in\{0,\dots,9\}\).

Removing the middle digit gives \(10a+c\), so:
\[
10a+c\equiv 0 \pmod 7.
\]
Since \(10\equiv 3\pmod 7\), we get
\[
c\equiv -3a\equiv 4a \pmod 7.
\]

Also \(N\equiv 0\pmod 7\):
\[
100a+10b+c\equiv 2a+3b+c\equiv 0\pmod 7.
\]
Substitute \(c\equiv -3a\pmod 7\):
\[
2a+3b-3a\equiv 0 \pmod 7
\]
\[
3b-a\equiv 0\pmod 7.
\]
Since \(3^{-1}\equiv 5\pmod 7\),
\[
b\equiv 5a\pmod 7.
\]

To minimize \(N\), take the smallest possible \(a=1\). Then:
\[
b\equiv 5\pmod 7 \Rightarrow b=5,
\]
\[
c\equiv 4\pmod 7 \Rightarrow c=4.
\]
Thus:
\[
N=100(1)+10(5)+4=154.
\]

Check: \(154\div 7=22\), and removing the middle digit gives \(14\), divisible by \(7\).

\[
\boxed{154}
\]
